verdict.rationale: RunAnywhere's own MetalRT engine uses Metal 3.1 GPU features on Apple Silicon and reports throughput figures (for example 184 tok/s on Llama-3.2-3B, winning 3 of 4 benchmarks against uzu). However, it requires M3 or later, and M1/M2 fall back to llama.cpp. Most of this evidence comes from HN thread replies rather than first-party docs. Missing for 10: M1/M2 Metal support, first-party documentation of the Metal/ARM optimizations, explicit evidence of native ARM (CPU) optimizations, independent benchmark corroboration.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can get accelerated inference on Apple Silicon via native ARM and Metal optimizations

citations.quote: MetalRT uses Metal 3.1 GPU features available on M3, M3 Pro, M3 Max, M4, and later chips. M1/M2 support is coming soon, falling back to open-source llama.cpp engine.
MetalRT wins 3 of 4 benchmarks. The bigger difference is MetalRT also handles STT and TTS natively
Accelerated by whatever silicon the device has.
validates every kernel against the silicon it runs on
